# stdx.route

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Typed routing descriptions: method/path patterns, stable names, body and
reply schemas, and handlers. Tables are validated (conflicts, malformed
patterns, duplicate names and parameters) before serving; URLs and
OpenAPI documents are derived from the same descriptions.

### `get`

```badger
fn get<E>(path: String, name: Symbol, handler: fn(http.Request, Params) -> Result<http.Response, E>) -> Route where E: Display, E: HttpStatus
```

### `get_json`

```badger
fn get_json<P, R, E>(path: String, name: Symbol, handler: fn(P) -> Result<R, E>) -> Route where P: Codec, R: Codec, E: Display, E: HttpStatus
```

A JSON GET route: the path's `:name`s (and the query's parameters)
decode into `P` (`{}` for none; numbers and booleans are parsed), and
the handler's reply is sent with status 200. An invalid parameter is a
structured 400 reply, an error the status it carries (`HttpStatus`).
For another status, use `typed`.

### `json`

```badger
fn json<B, R, E>(method: Symbol, path: String, name: Symbol, handler: fn(http.Request, Params, B) -> Result<(Int, R), E>) -> Route where B: Codec, R: Codec, E: Display, E: HttpStatus
```

A typed JSON route: the request body is validated against `B`'s schema
(a failure is a structured 400 reply naming the input path) and the
handler's `(status, reply)` is encoded with `R`'s schema. Both schemas
are part of the description (OpenAPI).

### `json_get`

```badger
fn json_get<R, E>(path: String, name: Symbol, handler: fn(http.Request, Params) -> Result<(Int, R), E>) -> Route where R: Codec, E: Display, E: HttpStatus
```

A typed JSON route without a request body.

### `openapi`

```badger
fn openapi(routes: List<Route>, title: String, version: String) -> Result<String, RouteError>
```

An OpenAPI 3.1 document for the table, from the same descriptions:
operation ids are route names, path parameters come from the patterns
(and query parameters from the other fields of a `get_json`-style
route's parameter type), and typed routes contribute their body/reply JSON Schemas.

### `params`

```badger
fn params(request: http.Request) -> Params
```

The query parameters of a request: `params.get("q")` for
`GET /search?q=bad`.

### `params_of`

```badger
fn params_of(path: String) -> List<String>
```

The `:name` parameters of a pattern, in order.

### `path_of`

```badger
fn path_of(uri: String) -> String
```

The path of a request URI, without its query string: `/search?q=bad`
becomes `/search`.

### `post_json`

```badger
fn post_json<P, B, R, E>(path: String, name: Symbol, handler: fn(P, B) -> Result<R, E>) -> Route where P: Codec, B: Codec, R: Codec, E: Display, E: HttpStatus
```

A JSON POST route: parameters as `get_json`, the body decodes into `B`
(an invalid body is a structured 400 reply), and the reply is sent with
status 201 (created).

### `query_of`

```badger
fn query_of(uri: String) -> Option<String>
```

The query string of a request URI (without the `?`), if it has one.

### `query_params`

```badger
fn query_params(uri: String) -> Params
```

The query parameters of a request URI (`?a=1&b=2`): the names and
values are percent-decoded. A parameter without a value (`?a`) has the
empty string as its value.

### `table`

```badger
fn table(routes: List<Route>) -> Result<http.Handler, RouteError>
```

Validate a route table and compile it into an HTTP handler.

### `typed`

```badger
fn typed<P, B, R, E>(method: Symbol, path: String, name: Symbol, handler: fn(http.Request, P, B) -> Result<(Int, R), E>) -> Route where P: Codec, B: Codec, R: Codec, E: Display, E: HttpStatus
```

A fully typed route: path parameters decode into `P` (a record whose
fields are the pattern's `:name`s; numbers and booleans are parsed), the
body into `B`, and the reply encodes `R`. Invalid parameters or bodies are
structured 400 replies; all three schemas are part of the description.

### `url`

```badger
fn url(routes: List<Route>, name: Symbol, params: Params) -> Result<String, RouteError>
```

Build the URL of a named route from its parameters. An unknown route,
a missing parameter, or an unexpected one is a structured error; values
are percent-encoded.

### `validate`

```badger
fn validate(routes: List<Route>) -> Result<Unit, RouteError>
```

Check a route table: names unique and present, paths well formed,
parameters named and unique, methods known, no two routes matching the
same requests.
